featured_reviews.name: Anmol Sanyasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
We went to Flavors at Bay near Hotel Hira mainly because it was convenient for us. Unfortunately, the food was a big disappointment.

I understand that it’s a vegetarian restaurant and spices are an important part of Indian cooking, but spices should complement the meal — not completely overpower it. Everything we ordered tasted like it was just packed with masala and nothing else.

We ordered momos, and they were honestly the worst part of the meal. They didn’t taste like real momos at all. Instead of a proper filling, it felt like a dough ball stuffed with pure spices. The taste matched how it looked — just overwhelming masala with no balance. Coming from a Nepali background where we eat momos often, this was really disappointing.

The biryani was the same story. It was mostly spice with very little flavor or balance beyond that.

The service itself was good and the staff were polite. The location was convenient for us as well. However, the restaurant felt quite empty and overall the food experience was not good. Unfortunately, the heavy spices even gave us heartburn afterwards.

We really wanted to enjoy the meal, but it ended up being a very disappointing experience.

The ambience is clean, calm, and perfect for both family dinners and casual outings. The staff is polite, attentive, and ensures quick service without compromising on quality. Every dish we tried was well-prepared, delicious, and beautifully presented.

What I really appreciated is their commitment to Jain food preparation standards while still maintaining rich taste and variety. The desserts were also a great highlight!

Overall, a fantastic place for anyone looking for pure veg and Jain cuisine with great taste and a pleasant dining atmosphere. Highly recommended for family meals and special occasions.

On reminding the new staff (as old staff had vanished), they punched in repeat item in our bill, even though delivery happened only once! Due to their poor service I had to pay for an extra Juice! Not a nice experience.
When we are big group, and several guests have multiple choice of food, it is difficult for us to track but I would expect the restaurant staff to be able to handle accurate billing for large group of guests.

On discussing the same with owner (Rahul Jain), he said he will look in the CCTV footage and refund my amount via UPI. On following up, he said he did not get time but will refund the amount. I shared him 2 different UPI however both time he said incorrect UPI.
Later he changes his statement that no extra payment was charged! And then again he says that visit our restaurant where he can pay me in cash.
Looking at this behaviour, i will not like to even like to recommend this place to anyone.

featured_reviews.name: Prem Raval
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a heart-winning experience at All in 1 - Pure Jain Restaurant near Opera House, Charni Road, Mumbai!

Since I follow Swaminarayan traditions and rituals, this was a comfort place in all aspects.

The ambience was truly heartwarming, with attention to detail that made the space feel welcoming and vibrant. It was very informative to learn about jain practices and rituals w.r.t food as illustrated on their diverse menu.

I tried a few dishes and was genuinely impressed:
- Burmese Khowsuey: perfectly done with authentic flavors, all Jain-friendly!
- Schezwan Pot Rice: hard to find a pure Jain version in Mumbai, and this one had incredibly fresh, juicy veggies.
- Chimichanga: my first time trying it, and I absolutely loved the burst of Mexican flavors.
- Goti Soda: classic Gujarati twist, especially refreshing in raw mango and guava flavors.

The owner (Nirav Bhai) and manager were both very warm and welcoming, which added so much to the experience.

And just when I thought it couldn’t get better, they served a delightful mukhwas (mouth freshener) to wrap up the meal, a perfect finishing touch.

I also learned about their initiative of Jain Food Festival and their upcoming plans for opening a small supermarket for fresh & authentic ingredients.

My personal ratings are as follows:
Food: 9/10
Price: 9/10
Drinks: 8/10
Service: 10/10
Quantity: 11/10
Location: 10/10
Ambience: 10/10
Authenticity: 10/10
Insta-worthy: 10/10
Vegetarian-Jain: 100/10

Definitely looking forward to visiting again! 🌱💛

featured_reviews.name: Jatin Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Iconic restaurant located at Charni Road, perhaps needs no introduction, was in the vicinity and was craving for some yummy Chaat and fast food! Shiv Krishna was our stop for that night. Named after two deities, one can expect it to be an all veg restaurant. The moment you enter the restaurant you can see beautiful paintings of Lord Krishna in various a avatars all over. Restaurant has two levels, upper deck has AC.

Talking about what all we had at Shiv Krishna -

As mentioned earlier was craving for some Chaat so we started with Sev Puri. Neatly presented to us. Sev Puri is usually famous of all street vendors and hawkers in Mumbai but you get a similar taste of it sitting in the comforts of this place. We followed it up with Veg Pizza. I would personally say it's made in the Indian way and I have no qualms in saying that I love the pizza made in this style. Very homely style and I enjoyed it.

Along with food, we ordered for couple of drinks - Paan Mojito and Kit Kat Shake. Mojito was refreshing with fresh Paan flavor. Good part is no essence. Kit Kat Shake was decent. Moving on, we next tried the famous Pav Bhaji of Shiv Sagar. It definitely features amongst the top selling list and most popular dish. Again presented in a very neat way. Was pretty stuffed by now, but the manager suggested us to also try the Tandoori Cheese Kulcha which is a relatively new dish introduced by the restaurant. Served in a starter format, so quite unique in its way. Stuffing is a mix of paneer and cheese mashed well and grilled well. Stuffed in Kulcha covering and kept in tandoor. Would recommend people to try this dish in case they haven't tried it elsewhere.

Last but not the least, was really excited to have the Cassatta ice-cream. Have had it really long back and was excited to see it as a part of the menu here. A combo of chocolate, tutti fruti, butter scotch ice-cream with nuts used for garnishing. Just loved the ice-cream and would love to revisit the place just for this again.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Kamat Govindashram in Girgaon is a legendary place for authentic Mumbai-style pav bhaji.
The taste is rich, well-balanced, and consistently good, made with quality ingredients and served hot with soft pav and generous butter. The bhaji has that classic old-school flavor which you rarely find these days.
Service is quick despite the place being crowded most of the time, and the staff is efficient. The ambience is simple and traditional, focusing more on food than fancy decor- which actually adds to its charm. Hygiene and cleanliness are well maintained.
Overall, it's a must-visit spot for pav bhaji lovers who want to experience the true taste of Mumbai. Worth every bite and every rupee.

Sukh Sagar is conveniently located just a 2-minute walk from Girgaon Chowpatty. We visited on a Saturday evening and had to wait about 10 minutes for a table, which was reasonable given the crowd.

We ordered dosa, uttapam, pizza, and pav bhaji. Unfortunately, the food didn’t meet our expectations. My mother felt the pav bhaji lacked flavor—as the saying goes, “unchi dukan, fiki pakwan” (big shop, bland food). Having tried authentic South Indian cuisine in Chennai and Kerala, I found Sukh Sagar’s dosa and uttapam fell short of that standard. The only dish that impressed us was the pizza.

The prices seemed quite high considering the taste and quality of the food. My mother, a senior citizen and excellent cook herself, jokingly remarked that she could prepare better food at home!

We will never come to this restaurant again.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Sukh Sagar for dinner in October 2025. While the food quality was excellent and we truly enjoyed the meal, there were a few significant drawbacks to the experience.
First, the pricing felt excessively high for the value provided. For instance, a single bottle of mineral water was priced at ₹50, which is considerably above the market rate. Second, the cleanliness of the seating area was disappointing. The seat covers appeared unwashed and were visibly dirty, suggesting they had not been cleaned recently.
On a positive note, the service was good and the staff was attentive. However, for a restaurant at this price point, I expected a much higher standard of hygiene and more reasonable pricing for basic items.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Form is awesome, content needs to match up to it & this team can do it!

Here are the things we loved :
- imaginative menu
- lovely ambiance
- friendly staff
- comes with an awesome reputation
- the Mahabaleshwar patties was super

Here are things that can be better:
- thanks to the reputation & first hand experience of Soam the expectation is very high and any lapse can make a big difference
- the food needs to match - the menu which is very thoughtful : few examples (1) Bharli Vangi served needed to be authentic, for the promise, expectation and price - what was served was deep fried brinjals mixed with green masala, which had lots of oil floating on it : Expectation was authentic stuffed / bharli brinjal (2) The Grandma’s fresh green chana - when we checked was dried green chana soaked overnight! The promise and the delivery needs to match (3) the Maharashtrian platter was super greasy and soaked in oil (4) The portions are abysmal- the Potli Biriyani was minuscule & the Jowar Roti accompanying the Bharli Brinjal were a tad bigger than poories!

All in all - you have built a great reputation, you have an awesome venue, we know you have the capability - please please please deliver on the quality, authenticity and portions of the food - that’s what we come there for in the first place

Please see this as a fans review - I want to come there often and enjoy the menu you have promised!

featured_reviews.name: Bomi Manekshaw
featured_reviews.review_text:
The concept of a high tea unlimited buffet would seem attractive to the Indian pallet. Most food items like the two bite burger or the singal piece sev puri are certainly not items to be eaten cold and stale in a buffet.
The service was pleasent but excruciatingly slow for the 90 plus year old ladies who visited more for the experience than to demonstrate their poor appetite. The only item that they thought would be worth having with a hot coffee or tea were the bhajiyas.

And, the staff tested the ladies patience of taking almost 30 minutes plus to heat and serve them. Thank God the flavour of the mango mousse in the tiny cutting chai glass was the saving grace for these oldies. But, at ₹725/- (including taxes) per person this was certainly more premium a price for being next to the Bhavan's and Wilson College clientele than the food, service or lounging.

While the decore has some antique stuff like the ancient telephone ... overall they have the opportunity to work a lot on the atmosphere too.

featured_reviews.name: Kiyansh Shukla
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vanakkam Vihar, located right opposite the iconic Royal Opera House in Girgaon, is a reliable, bustling spot for anyone craving solid, comforting South Indian comfort food in South Mumbai. Whether you are wrapping up a beach stroll at nearby Girgaon Chowpatty or stepping out after a show at the Opera House, this multi-level pure-vegetarian restaurant offers a welcoming and clean environment.
Here is a comprehensive look at what to expect:
The Vibe & Ambiance
The restaurant balances traditional charm with a modern, spacious casual-dining setup. The ground floor features comfortable high and low seating, while the upper level ("Firangi") branches out into multi-cuisine options. The space is well-lit, fully air-conditioned, and remarkably clean, making it highly family-friendly. The staff adds a touch of authenticity by dressing in traditional South Indian attire.
What to Order
While the massive menu extends to North Indian dishes and street-side snacks, the absolute highlight here remains their coastal and southern delicacies.
The Dosas: Their Kara Masala Dosa and Chettinad Dosa are beautifully crisp, served with generous portions of fresh coconut chutney, a tangy tomato-garlic chutney, and piping hot sambar. If you are looking for something lighter, the Neer Dosa and fluffy Appams paired with a rich veggie stew or Malabari curry are top-tier.
The Idli Platters: Beyond standard idlis, their Podi Idli (tossed in a vibrant, spiced gun powder and ghee) and the signature Thalaiva Idli are highly recommended.
Filter Coffee: No meal here is complete without their authentic Filter Coffee. It is served strong, perfectly frothy, and features that robust, traditional chicory-coffee blend.
Jain Options: For those with dietary restrictions, the restaurant stands out for offering a robust, dedicated selection of highly flavorful Jain South Indian variants.

The drinks were very refreshing specially the orange sunrise mocktail and the pink Lady Smoothie was so good.

Overall was a great experience with great ambience and the service which they provided was amazing

featured_reviews.name: Swad Stories
featured_reviews.review_text: There is no need to give introduction to Achija. One of the well known brands for fastfoods in Mumbai since more than 50 years. We went to one of their outlets in Lower Parel. Very nice ambience and food as alwys delicious. We went just for a midnight snacking as this place is usually open till 2 in the night. We tried a few variety in soup like Manchow, Veg Mexican soup and veg clear soup. The taste was really nice specially the Mexican soup. We had their classic veg cheese pizza and pav bhaji. Nothing much to say for the taste as they have alwys maintained a class in taste. Overall a good experience and a good place to be.

featured_reviews.name: Ria Jain
featured_reviews.review_text: Now I get why everyone loves Achija! The food here is pure deliciousness in every bite. Their pav bhaji is buttery & Cheesy (One of the Best pav bhaji) the pizzas are loaded with cheese ( Indian Desi taste ) and the North Indian dishes are super rich flavorful. The ambience is lively, service is quick, and the vibe makes it a perfect spot for both casual hangouts and family dinners. Definitely one of Lower Parel’s must-visit places

featured_reviews.name: Jay Sondagar
featured_reviews.review_text: Perhaps one of The Best Pure Veg restaurant in Mumbai that is open till late night (1.30 am). The Kulcha is super delicious and order any food and you can feel the authentic and premium quality taste. It felt like Each vegetable in the sabji, including the cut lemon and tomatoes in the salad bowl is handpicked and assorted! Genuine quality ingredients. The flavours bursts in mouth does give you a feel which you rarely experience in hotel. A must must try. Swaminarayan/Jain/Half Jain options are also available. The complimentary spicy Papad with Green chutney is worth to kill the little wait till the food arrives. Staff is also so courteous. If you ever go to visit phoenix palladium mall, don’t come back without having a dinner/lunch there.
